subject: biology-1
question: A researcher labels a pair of **homologous chromosomes**, one from the father red and one from the mother blue, and follows them through meiosis. In which division do the red and blue chromosomes first separate into different cells?
explanation: Homologous chromosomes are the members of each matched pair, and they are pulled apart during anaphase I, when the cell's chromosome number drops from diploid to haploid. B describes the separation of sister chromatids, which are copies of the same chromosome and therefore the same color. A and D are stages of meiosis II, by which time the red and blue chromosomes are already in different cells.
